title: Revert per-job dockerd bounce (bc724ee) — caused /run hook timeout
description: The post-restore dockerd bounce added in bc724ee blocks the /run hook 200 ack for ~28s (full containerd+buildkit reboot, not the assumed 1-2s), exceeding Lambda's run-hook ack window and killing the MicroVM before the runner starts. Original symptom it fixed was only cosmetic BuildKit healthcheck log noise. Revert bc724ee to restore the warm-snapshot daemon with no bounce.

title: Fix DNS resolution for nested Docker builds in MicroVM (loopback resolver)
description: Jobs that run 'docker build' fail with pip '[Errno -2] Name or service not known'. Root cause: the MicroVM host /etc/resolv.conf has only 'nameserver 127.0.0.2' (Lambda's loopback DNS proxy). It works from the host netns but is unreachable from container netns; Docker strips the loopback nameserver and falls back to 8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4, which this VPC blocks. MTU is fine (eth0=9001 > docker0=1500). Fix: bake dnsmasq into the image, start it bound to the docker0 gateway 172.17.0.1 (--bind-dynamic) forwarding upstream to 127.0.0.2, and start dockerd with --dns 172.17.0.1. Both processes must be children of app.js so they are snapshot-warmed. Remove/gate the temporary network diagnostics once verified.
acceptance_criteria: A workflow job running 'docker build' that pip-installs from PyPI succeeds inside the MicroVM; container DNS resolves via 172.17.0.1 -> 127.0.0.2; debug diagnostics removed or gated.
notes: VERIFIED at runtime. BuildKit DNS probe in a real 'docker build' resolved pypi.org via Server 172.17.0.1 (the exact '#5 [2/2] RUN' path that was failing). Diagnostics removed; fix is dnsmasq (Dockerfile) + startDnsmasq()/--dns 172.17.0.1 (app.js). Diagnostic-only packages (iproute2/dnsutils/iputils-ping) also reverted. Gates green (tsc clean, jest 23/23).
close_reason: DNS fix verified: nested BuildKit 'docker build' resolves DNS via the dnsmasq forwarder on 172.17.0.1. Root cause (loopback-only 127.0.0.2 resolver unreachable from container netns) resolved.

title: Bounce dockerd after MicroVM restore to fix BuildKit session healthcheck
description:
The snapshot-warmed dockerd carries frozen gRPC/session sockets that cannot survive memory snapshot/restore. After restore, BuildKit's session healthcheck dials the dead, never-released connection slot and logs perpetual 'session healthcheck failed fatally: only one connection allowed' errors. Builds still succeed (fresh per-build sessions), but the daemon's frozen session slot produces continuous noise.

Option B fix: restart dockerd at job time (after restore, before the runner starts) so the build engine is born post-restore with clean sessions. Overlay2 layers are on disk so the bounce costs ~1-2s vs the ~1min build-time warm-up that the snapshot still saves. Add timing logs to both the build-phase warm-up and the run-phase restart for validation.
acceptance_criteria: dockerd is killed and re-spawned in app.js /run handler before entrypoint.sh; waits for readiness before starting the runner; best-effort (does not block non-docker jobs on failure); build-phase warm-up and run-phase restart both emit elapsed-ms timing logs; dnsmasq survives the bounce; comments updated to reflect per-job restart; npm run build + npm test pass.
close_reason: Verified Option B: per-job dockerd bounce in /run handler post-restore; shared waitForDockerReady/spawnDockerDaemon helpers; restartingDocker gates intentional exits; restartingDocker reset (finally) before fresh spawn so new daemon's exit handler stays live; SIGKILL fallback timer cleared on exit; null/exited-daemon path still respawns; startDockerDaemon() rejection handled at module load; build-time readiness still gates /ready; timing logs on success+timeout for both phases; dnsmasq not bounced. npm run build + npm test (23) pass.
